Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:12:1.hebrew: מהו לעמוד - מי מיחייב למיקם, או לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:12:1.english: What is [the law as to] standing - Is one obligated to stand, or not?

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:13:1.hebrew: תורה עומדת מפני לומדיה - בתמיה: לפי שעסוקים בדבר הלכה היו, קרי להו לדידהו תורה עצמה, ולדידיה קרי לומדיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:13:1.english: The Torah stands before those who study it - [This is said] as a rhetorical question: Because they were engaged in a matter of Halakhah, he called them the Torah itself, and he called himself those who study it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:14:1.hebrew: לייט עלה אביי - אהך דרבי אלעזר, כל מאן דציית ליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:14:1.english: Abaye cursed regarding it - Regarding that [ruling] of Rabbi Elazar, [namely,] anyone who obeys him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:15:1.hebrew: כדאיתא - משום דדבר מגונה הוא, לא רצה לפרסמה. והרי הוא מפורש במדרש רבי תנחומא: ראו כמה עבים שוקיו, כמה צוארו שמן — הכל משלנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:15:1.english: As it is - Because it is a disgraceful matter, [the Gemara] did not wish to publicize it. But behold, it is explained in Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma: “See how thick his thighs are, how fat his neck is — [it is] all from ours!”

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:16:1.hebrew: עומד מלפניו - משמתחיל ליכנס לתוך ארבע אמות, ואינו יושב עד שיעבור הימנו ארבע אמות השניות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:16:1.english: One stands before him - From [the moment the scholar] begins to enter within four cubits [of him], and one does not sit until [the scholar] passes four cubits beyond him — the second four cubits.

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:16:2.english: As it is stated: “And they looked after Moses” - And Moses was a nasi.

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:1:1.hebrew: מכבוד שמים - שהרי פני יוצרו אינו מקבל אלא שחרית וערבית. הלכך, מי שעומד מפני רבו שחרית, אינו רשאי לעמוד מפניו אלא ערבית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:1:1.english: Than the honor of Heaven - For one welcomes the presence of his Creator only in the morning and in the evening. Therefore, one who stands before his teacher in the morning is permitted to stand before him only in the evening as well.

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:2:1.hebrew: אמאי לא - מאי טרחא איכא? אורחא דמילתא הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:2:1.english: Why not - What trouble is there? It is the normal way of things.

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:2:2.english: He should not trouble [them] - This is our reading.

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:3:1.hebrew: וטוב לא יהיה לרשע - אין טוב אלא תורה, שנאמר: "כי לקח טוב", אלמא תלמודו משתכח. "ולא יאריך ימים אלא כצל" — מה טעם? לפי שאינו ירא מלפני ה', ומורא זו קימה היא, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:3:1.english: And it shall not be well for the wicked - “Good” is nothing other than Torah, as it is stated: “For I have given you good instruction; [do not forsake My teaching]” (Proverbs 4:2) — thus, his learning is forgotten. “Neither shall he prolong his days, [which are] as a shadow” — what is the reason? Because he does not fear before God. And this fear is standing, as [the Gemara] proceeds to explain.

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:4:1.hebrew: מוראת רבית - דגבי רבית נמי כתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:ל״ו) אל תקח מאתו וגו' ויראת, וכן גבי משקלות (דברים כ״ה:ט״ו) אבן שלמה וצדק וכו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:4:1.english: Fear of interest - For with regard to interest it is also written: (Leviticus 25:36) “Do not take from him [interest], etc., and you shall fear [your God]”; and likewise with regard to weights: (Deuteronomy 25:15) “A perfect and just weight, etc.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:4:2.hebrew: פני פני גמר - כתיב הכא ״מלפני״, וכתיב התם (ויקרא יט): ״מפני שיבה״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:4:2.english: He derived [a verbal analogy between] “penei” [and] “penei” - It is written here: “[Because he does not fear] before [millifnei God]” (Ecclesiastes 8:13), and it is written there (Leviticus 19:32): “Before [mipenei] the hoary head [you shall rise up].”

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:5:1.english: And he is his teacher - The son is his father's teacher.

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:5:2.hebrew: מקמי אבוך - ואע"ג דרב יהודה רביה דרב יחזקאל אבוה הוה, כדאמרי' לעיל (קידושין דף לב.): "אבא, לא תתנייא הכי":
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:5:2.english: Before your father - Even though Rav Yehuda was the teacher of his father, Rav Yeḥezkel, as we said above (Kiddushin 32a): "Father, do not teach it this way."

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:6:1.hebrew: אלא מאי קאמר ליה - אמאי צריך לאזהוריה, אי לאו למילף מינה הוראה בעלמא, דאף על פי שהוא רבו, חייב לעמוד מפניו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:6:1.english: Rather, what is he saying to him - Why did [Shmuel] need to instruct [Rav Yehuda], if not to derive from it a general ruling that even though he is his teacher, he is obligated to stand before him?

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:7:1.hebrew: אני איני כדאי לעמוד מפני בני - קס"ד דה"ק: אני רבו של בני, ולא הייתי כדי לעמוד מפניו אלא מפני שנתחתן בנשיא. ומדקאמר "אני איני כדי", ש"מ דאילו היה כדי — שהיה תלמידו — הוה ליה למיקם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:7:1.english: It is not appropriate for me to stand before my son - [The Gemara] initially thought that this is what he is saying: I am my son's teacher, and it would not be appropriate for me to stand before him except that he married into [the household of] the Nasi. And from [the fact] that he says, "It is not appropriate for me [to stand]," conclude from this that if it were appropriate — in that he was his student — he would have had to stand.

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:8:1.hebrew: ה"ק - כלומר, "איני כדי" דקאמר, לאו משום גדולת תורה הוא, אלא מפני שהוא אביו קאמר, דאין אב כדי לעמוד מפני הבן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:8:1.english: This is what he is saying - That is to say, that which he said, "I am not fitting," is not on account of greatness in Torah; rather, he said [it] because he is his father, for a father is not [fitting] to stand before [his] son.

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:9:1.hebrew: רכוב כמהלך דמי - רבו רכוב — כמהלך דמי, וצריך לעמוד מפניו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:9:1.english: Is [one who is] riding considered like walking - [If] his teacher is riding, is he considered like [one who is] walking, and [one] must stand before him?

Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:9:2.hebrew: או לאו - כמהלך דמי, אלא כיושב — דבתריה דידיה אזלינן, והא קא יתיב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 33b:9:2.english: Or not - [considered] like one walking, but rather like one sitting, for we follow him himself, and behold, he is sitting.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 33b:1:1.hebrew: אין תלמיד חכם רשאי לעמוד מפני רבו אלא שחרית וערבית - תימה: למה איקפיד רבא לעיל? שמא קמו מפניו שחרית וערבית, ולאו אדעתיה! ונראה לפרש, דדין זה אינו נוהג אלא באותם הדרין בבית הרב, דמסתמא עמדו שחרית וערבית; אבל תלמידים אחרים חייבין לעמוד אפי' מאה פעמים ביום, שמא יראה אחר ויחשדם. ואפילו אותם שדרין בבית הרב נמי, אם באו פנים חדשות — צריכין לעמוד:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 33b:1:1.english: A Torah scholar is permitted to stand before his teacher only morning and evening - [This is] puzzling: Why was Rava upset above? Perhaps they had stood before him morning and evening, and he was not aware [of it]! And it seems [correct] to explain that this ruling applies only to those who reside in the teacher's house, for they presumably stood [before him] morning and evening; but other students are obligated to stand even one hundred times a day, lest someone else see [them] and suspect them [of disrespect]. And even those who reside in the teacher's house as well, if new faces have arrived, they are required to stand.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 33b:1:2.hebrew: [אין ת"ח כו' - תימה: וכי כל הני דלעיל מיירי בלא קמו שחרית וערבית? וצ"ל: "אינו רשאי" — "אינו חייב", כדפי' לעיל.] ת"י:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 33b:1:2.english: ["A Torah scholar is not permitted, etc." - This is puzzling: Did all those [cases] mentioned above deal with [situations where] they had not stood in the morning and evening? And one must say: "He is not permitted" [means] "he is not obligated," as explained above.] — Tosafot Yeshanim.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 33b:4:1.hebrew: ואימא מורא משקלות - פירש בקונטרס: גבי משקלות כתיב (דברים כ״ה:ט״ו) "אבן שלמה וצדק יהיה לך". וקשה, דלא מצינו בשום מקום דכתיב בהו מורא בהדיא. ויש גורסים "מכשולות", דכתיב (ויקרא י״ט:י״ד) "ולפני עור לא תתן מכשול ויראת". וא"ת: א"כ, מאי משני "פני" "פני" גמר? גבי מכשול נמי כתיב "לפני עור לא תתן מכשול"! וי"ל: דלא דמי, דעמידה מפני זקן שייך לירא מפני השם, כדאמר (ב"ק דף מא:) "את ה' אלהיך תירא" — לרבות ת"ח. ור' יצחק מפרש דמצינו מורא במשקלות, כדאמרי' במדרש: "זכור את אשר עשה לך עמלק... ואתה עיף ויגע ולא ירא אלהים" — היינו בשביל המשקלות, ועל עון זה בא עמלק, דבתר פרשת משקלות כתיב "זכור את אשר עשה לך עמלק" בפרשת כי תצא. והיינו דכתיב במשלי: "מאזני מרמה תועבת ה' ואבן שלמה רצונו", וסמוך ליה "בא זדון ויבא קלון", כלומר שעל עון זה בא זדון וקלון של עמלק:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 33b:4:1.english: "And say [that it refers to] fear [stated with regard to] weights" - Rashi explained that with regard to weights it is written (Deuteronomy 25:15): "A perfect and just weight shall you have." And this is difficult, for we do not find anywhere that "fear" is explicitly written regarding them. And some have the reading "stumbling blocks," as it is written (Leviticus 19:14): "And before a blind person you shall not place a stumbling block, and you shall fear [your God]." And if you say: If so, how does [the Gemara] answer that he derives [it via a verbal analogy of] "penei" [from] "penei"? With regard to a stumbling block it is also written: "Before [lifnei] a blind person you shall not place a stumbling block"! And one can say: It is not comparable, for standing before an elder is related to fearing God, as [the Gemara] says (Bava Kamma 41b): "'You shall fear the Lord your God' — to include Torah scholars." And Rabbi Yitzchak explains that we do find "fear" with regard to weights, as we say in the Midrash: "'Remember what Amalek did to you... and you were faint and weary, and he feared not God' (Deuteronomy 25:17–18) — that is on account of the weights, and because of this sin Amalek came, for after the section of weights it is written: 'Remember what Amalek did to you' in Parashat Ki Teitzei. And this is what is written in Proverbs (11:1–2): 'A false balance is an abomination to the Lord, but a perfect weight is His delight,' and adjacent to it [is written]: 'When presumption comes, then comes shame,' meaning that on account of this sin came the presumption and shame of Amalek.
